name: Tiny laptops and remote desktops
description: Remote desktops arranged like a miniature laptop. A separate, reachable Mac or PC does the computing; supported hosts and setup vary.

name: Desktop workspaces and terminals
description: Local workspaces, PC emulation and remote terminals. These are different ways to work: check the entry and laptop guide for where computation runs.

name: Notes and writing
description: Notebooks, sketches and writing tools adapted to the fold or expanded display.

name: Documents and PDFs
description: Compare, edit and sign documents with more room for pages and controls.

name: Planning and focus
description: Calendars, tasks and timers that use the extra space or a propped-up pose.

name: Reading and research
description: Feeds, saved articles and visual thinking. Some entries document layout support without a unique hinge interaction.

name: Photos and video
description: Capture, edit, watch and present using the available displays and poses.

name: Music and instruments
description: Turn the hinge into an instrument or the screen into a miniature music player.

name: Games
description: Fold-controlled games, tabletop boards and documented Duo layout adaptations. Specific hinge mechanics are stated only where sourced.

name: Playful objects and art
description: Small surprises that make the physical shape of the phone part of the experience.

name: Fitness and outdoors
description: Workout dashboards and outdoor tools with documented Duo layouts.

name: Weather and nature
description: Use the expanded display for forecasts, maps and comparisons.

name: Travel and navigation
description: Plan a journey or follow it with layouts that adapt to the phone.

name: Communication
description: Messages and collaboration with documented Duo support.

name: Cooking and everyday
description: Everyday workflows made more useful by the folding display.

name: Utilities and measurements
description: Hinge measurements and small tools with a documented Duo-specific use.

name: Source projects and experiments
description: Source projects and research prototypes, separate from ordinary downloads. A prototype may have no public build; code availability does not establish an open-source license or successful hardware testing.

name: Previews and watchlist
description: Promising ideas whose availability is beta, announced or unconfirmed. A demo or developer claim is not a released feature.
